operations.content:
name: Fork native preview (build only)

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: Unsigned preview version (leave empty for a unique run version)
        required: false
        type: string
      windows_target:
        description: Windows delivery format (ZIP supports side-by-side validation)
        required: true
        default: nsis
        type: choice
        options:
          - nsis
          - zip

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: fork-native-preview
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  PREVIEW_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version || format('0.1.11-preview.{0}.{1}', github.run_number, github.run_attempt) }}
  PRODUCT_BASE: 59651c1761f6c63e9b6056839067066968e6a406
  T3CODE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: ""
  T3CODE_CLERK_JWT_TEMPLATE: ""
  T3CODE_CLERK_CLI_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID: ""
  T3CODE_RELAY_URL: ""
  CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY: "false"

jobs:
  linux:
    name: Linux x64 WSL runtime
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - name: Checkout exact source without credentials or vendored gitlinks
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git init .
          git remote add origin "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY.git"
          git fetch --no-tags origin "$GITHUB_SHA" "$PRODUCT_BASE"
          git sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' '!/.repos/'
          git checkout --detach "$GITHUB_SHA"
      - uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@250f29ce396baf5e8f24498e17c0dfdebabc26eb
        with:
          node-version-file: package.json
          run-install: false
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@6bed0761d98439e5a578e2877258200ad565ba87
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          targets: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
      - name: Install locked build dependencies
        run: vp install --frozen-lockfile --filter=@t3tools/desktop... --filter=t3... --filter=@t3tools/scripts...
      - name: Align preview version and build JS
        run: |
          node scripts/update-release-package-versions.ts "$PREVIEW_VERSION"
          vp run --filter t3 build
      - name: Build native resource monitor
        run: |
          cargo build --locked --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --manifest-path native/resource-monitor/Cargo.toml
          mkdir -p preview-monitor/linux-x64
          cp native/resource-monitor/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/t3-resource-monitor preview-monitor/linux-x64/
      - name: Build Linux single-executable
        run: node apps/server/scripts/cli.ts build-exe --verbose
      - name: Install the Linux archive build prerequisite
        run: command -v patchelf || { sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y patchelf; }
      - name: Package and smoke the WSL runtime
        run: |
          node scripts/build-cli-archive.ts --platform linux --arch x64 --version "$PREVIEW_VERSION" --resource-monitor-dir preview-monitor --output-dir preview-linux
          node scripts/smoke-cli-archive.ts --archive "preview-linux/t3-$PREVIEW_VERSION-linux-x64.tar.gz" --expect-version "$PREVIEW_VERSION"
          node scripts/fork-preview-manifest.mjs --directory preview-linux --target linux-x64 --version "$PREVIEW_VERSION"
      - name: Upload runtime and provenance
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        with:
          name: fork-preview-linux-x64
          path: preview-linux/*
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

  windows:
    name: Windows x64 desktop
    needs: linux
    runs-on: windows-2025
    timeout-minutes: 60
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: pwsh
        working-directory: C:\t3\s
    env:
      WINDOWS_TARGET: ${{ inputs.windows_target || 'nsis' }}
      TEMP: C:\t3\tmp
      TMP: C:\t3\tmp
      TMPDIR: C:\t3\tmp
    steps:
      - name: Checkout exact source into a short path
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\t3\s, C:\t3\tmp | Out-Null
          Set-Location C:\t3\s
          git init .
          git remote add origin "$env:GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$env:GITHUB_REPOSITORY.git"
          git fetch --no-tags origin $env:GITHUB_SHA $env:PRODUCT_BASE
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Checkout fetch failed' }
          git sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' '!/.repos/'
          git checkout --detach $env:GITHUB_SHA
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Checkout failed' }
      - uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@250f29ce396baf5e8f24498e17c0dfdebabc26eb
        with:
          node-version-file: C:/t3/s/package.json
          cache: false
          run-install: false
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@6bed0761d98439e5a578e2877258200ad565ba87
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          targets: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
      - name: Install Spectre-mitigated MSVC libraries
        run: |
          $vswhere = "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe"
          $installPath = & $vswhere -products * -latest -property installationPath
          $setup = "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\setup.exe"
          $result = Start-Process -FilePath $setup -ArgumentList 'modify','--installPath',"`"$installPath`"",'--add','Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Runtimes.x86.x64.Spectre','--quiet','--norestart' -Wait -PassThru -NoNewWindow
          if ($result.ExitCode -ne 0) { throw "MSVC setup failed: $($result.ExitCode)" }
      - name: Install locked dependencies
        run: |
          vp install --frozen-lockfile --filter=@t3tools/desktop... --filter=t3... --filter=@t3tools/scripts...
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Dependency installation failed' }
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c
        with:
          name: fork-preview-linux-x64
          path: C:\t3\wsl
      - name: Verify embedded runtime input and align versions
        run: |
          $manifest = Get-Content C:\t3\wsl\manifest.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
          if ($manifest.buildCommit -ne $env:GITHUB_SHA -or $manifest.productBase -ne $env:PRODUCT_BASE -or $manifest.target -ne 'linux-x64' -or $manifest.version -ne $env:PREVIEW_VERSION) { throw 'WSL provenance mismatch' }
          $archive = "C:\t3\wsl\t3-$env:PREVIEW_VERSION-linux-x64.tar.gz"
          $expected = @($manifest.artifacts | Where-Object { $_.name -eq (Split-Path $archive -Leaf) })
          if ($expected.Count -ne 1) { throw 'Missing or ambiguous WSL archive identity' }
          if ((Get-FileHash $archive -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower() -ne $expected.sha256) { throw 'WSL digest mismatch' }
          node scripts/update-release-package-versions.ts $env:PREVIEW_VERSION
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Version transform failed' }
      - name: Build isolated unsigned Windows preview
        run: |
          if ($env:WINDOWS_TARGET -notin @('nsis', 'zip')) { throw 'Unsupported Windows preview target' }
          node scripts/build-desktop-artifact.ts --platform win --arch x64 --target $env:WINDOWS_TARGET --fork-preview --build-version $env:PREVIEW_VERSION --wsl-runtime "C:\t3\wsl\t3-$env:PREVIEW_VERSION-linux-x64.tar.gz" --output-dir C:\t3\release --keep-stage --verbose
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Windows packaging failed' }
          node scripts/fork-preview-manifest.mjs --directory C:\t3\release --target windows-x64 --version $env:PREVIEW_VERSION --wsl-archive "C:\t3\wsl\t3-$env:PREVIEW_VERSION-linux-x64.tar.gz"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Manifest verification failed' }
      - name: Upload Windows preview and provenance
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        with:
          name: fork-preview-windows-x64
          path: |
            C:\t3\release\*.exe
            C:\t3\release\*.zip
            C:\t3\release\manifest.json
            C:\t3\release\SHA256SUMS
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

# Personal fork native previews

These are unsigned personal previews of stable `v0.1.11`, not releases.
Each artifact's generated `manifest.json` records the full upstream product-base
commit, actual build commit, source-overlay paths, version-only release transform,
and artifact hashes. Historical v0.0.42 evidence does not qualify this port.

## Isolation and limits

Build desktop artifacts with `--fork-preview` and a preview version such as
`0.1.11-preview.20261123.1`. The installer identity is
`com.tesseracode.t3code.preview`, named **T3 Code Fork Preview**.

The packaged bootstrap selects `~/.t3-fork-preview`, with Electron state below
its `electron` directory. It ignores an ambient ordinary T3 home and refuses
known live-profile paths. For an owned test directory, set
`T3CODE_FORK_PREVIEW_HOME` before launching. Do not set it to an existing install.
The preview keeps a separate single-instance lock, disables automatic updates
and does not register the stock T3 URL schemes.
Its runtime application name remains fork-specific after startup branding,
not just in the installer.
Preview startup does not import V1 local storage from stock profiles. Existing
storage in the same preview profile is retained; updating a build does not clear
previously imported data. Use a fresh owned preview home when qualifying isolation.

Desktop cloud OAuth and native passkeys are intentionally unavailable in this
isolated unsigned profile. Use local/direct connections. Do not use managed
remote installation/update flows against an existing production environment.
Provider sessions use their configured provider homes; choose separate homes
for isolation. Automated checks must disable providers or use owned provider
homes and must not run provider turns.

WSL uses its Linux user's `~/.t3-fork-preview` for both data and runtime cache.
The Windows path is never forwarded as the Linux data directory. Runtime
installation, pruning and invalidation stay outside the stock WSL cache.
Account-home probes send their shell script on stdin, avoiding Windows/WSL
argument re-quoting. They read the Linux account database, not an inherited
`HOME`. A failed probe stops isolated startup rather than using the ordinary
profile; its transport/exit details are logged.

## Linux and WSL runtime prerequisites

A bundled Node runtime is not a fully static Linux executable. The v0.1.11
archive builder copies `libatomic.so.1` and its license into the archive and
uses `patchelf` to set the executable's `RUNPATH` to `$ORIGIN/lib`. On a
pristine WSL image, a missing `libatomic.so.1` is a packaging failure: check
the archive contents and `RUNPATH` before installing host packages.

Qualify the actual target image, not just a build runner with compiler libraries
already installed. Preserve a missing-library failure as pristine-image evidence,
record the exact packages/versions subsequently installed, and label the resulting
checks as a dependency-installed variant. Installing a prerequisite does not by
itself prove managed startup, cache repair, native provider execution or migration.

## Build

Use the Node and pnpm versions declared in the root `package.json`, with the existing
native prerequisites in the development runbook. In a
dedicated build checkout, install locked dependencies, then use
`scripts/update-release-package-versions.ts` to align the four release manifests.
Do not commit that build-time version transform.

```sh
node scripts/build-desktop-artifact.ts \
  --platform mac --arch arm64 --target dmg \
  --build-version 0.1.11-preview.20261123.1 --fork-preview --keep-stage
node scripts/fork-preview-manifest.mjs \
  --directory release --target mac-arm64 --version 0.1.11-preview.20261123.1 \
  --product-base v0.1.11
```

Windows uses the same builder with `--platform win --arch x64 --target nsis`
and `--wsl-runtime <matching-linux-x64-archive>`. Build the Linux single-executable
and archive on Linux using the existing CLI builders, then smoke it before
embedding it. The build verifies the reviewed native dependency closure,
Windows payload budget, and embedded archive digest; those gates are not optional.

`.github/workflows/fork-native-preview.yml` is manual-dispatch-only and build-only.
There are no push, tag, pull-request, scheduled or reusable-workflow triggers.
It uploads Linux and
Windows artifacts without release tags, npm publication, signing or deployment.
The approved preview batch permits at most **four build-only CI attempts per target**
(Linux x64 and Windows x64), including reruns and new dispatches. Record each
attempt's run URL, exact source commit, target, result and remaining budget before
retrying; never retry automatically. The parent/integration operator owns dispatch.
Changing the upstream port does not reset that allowance.
The upstream release and signed macOS PR-preview workflows are not appropriate:
they can publish or sign.

## Install, inspect and roll back

Verify `SHA256SUMS` before using a download. Mac previews can be copied from the
DMG to a separately named application location. Windows installs under the fork
preview identity, not the ordinary app identity. Unsigned downloads may show OS
warnings; never disable Gatekeeper or SmartScreen globally.

First launch should show **T3 Code Fork Preview**, a fresh profile and TWS disabled.
Check the native environment before adding a separate test project. On Windows,
exercise WSL explicitly in Connections and confirm it is a distinct environment.
The independently smoked Linux archive alone does not qualify WSL integration.

Quit only the preview, then uninstall/remove that preview application to roll
back. Preserve `~/.t3-fork-preview` unless deliberately discarding preview work;
do not copy it over the normal profile. Do not mix backend versions against the
same database.

Build success, CLI smoke, native UI checks and receiving-host Windows/WSL
qualification are separate gates. Keep unrun gates marked pending. No artifacts
from this workflow are a signed/notarized release or an automatic update.

## Required qualification report

Attach actual manifests, hashes and command transcripts, not reconstructed
snapshots. Report separately:

- Native macOS arm64 candidate build and explicitly authorized UI verification.
- Linux x64 build and archive smoke on native Linux.
- Windows x64 installer execution, complete unpacked-application file count
  (maximum **80**), native dependency load and separate preview instance/profile.
- Receiving-host WSL/Ubuntu cold installation, executable `copilot`/`rg`/`tgrep`
  modes, warm-cache reuse and repair, account-home probing, and isolated state.
- Native Copilot session continuity on each receiving host, using authorized,
  isolated provider homes; automated packaging must not run provider turns.

An unavailable Windows/WSL/Ubuntu receiving host is **pending**, not passed.
POSIX readiness fixtures on macOS and archive smoke do not qualify installed WSL.
Self-containment probes must run where no ancestor `node_modules` is visible;
the builder deliberately refuses otherwise. If filesystem policy permits only
an in-worktree directory, report that gate as blocked instead of weakening it.
